title: PROCA: Programmable Probabilistic Processing Unit Architecture with Accept/Reject Prediction & Multicore Pipelining for Causal Inference
problem: Markov Chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) algorithms for probabilistic programming and causal inference are extremely compute-intensive and inherently sequential, preventing effective parallelization on CPUs and GPUs; existing MCMC accelerators are not programmable across arbitrary posterior distribution forms.
motivation: Causal inference and Bayesian probabilistic programming are growing in importance for data science and cognitive AI, but MCMC's sequential accept/reject sampling and arbitrary posterior computation create a performance wall that neither general-purpose nor prior domain-specific hardware has adequately addressed with both flexibility and efficiency.
method: PROCA is a specialized hardware processor for MCMC algorithms (Markov Chain Monte Carlo - a statistical method where each sample depends on the previous one). The processor uses processing-in-memory function units to generate samples, and it's programmable to handle any posterior distribution form from software probabilistic programming frameworks. The speed-up comes from a prediction step: PROCA predicts whether a proposed sample will be accepted before the full evaluation completes, starting computation on the next sample while still finalizing the current accept/reject decision. This prediction breaks MCMC's inherent sequential dependency, enabling multiple processor cores to work in parallel on different samples.
key_novelty: PROCA breaks MCMC's sequential dependency by predicting accept/reject decisions before they're fully computed, enabling multiple cores to process samples in parallel using processing-in-memory function units.
contributions: PROCA programmable MCMC processing unit with PIM-based sample generation supporting arbitrary posterior distributions.
Novel accept/reject prediction method that enables multi-core pipelining of otherwise sequential MCMC computation.
172-4871x speedup over Intel Xeon Gold CPU and 42-1058x speedup over NVIDIA A100 GPU across 9 benchmarks.
1.765x speedup and 9.47x energy efficiency improvement over state-of-the-art MCMC domain-specific accelerators.

metrics.speedup: 172-4871x over Intel Xeon Gold CPU; 42-1058x over NVIDIA A100 GPU; 1.765x over SOTA MCMC accelerator
metrics.energy_or_tops_w: 9.47x energy efficiency over SOTA MCMC accelerators

limitations: The accept/reject prediction accuracy and its impact on statistical correctness (chain mixing) across diverse posterior distributions is not quantified in the abstract.
primary_theme: Programmable PIM-based MCMC accelerator with accept/reject prediction for causal inference
